title: Calling detectChanges on parent during child's ngOnChanges leads to hooks not called

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Indicates than the issue relates to something that worked in a previous version

labels.name: area: core
labels.description: Issues related to the framework runtime

**Current behavior**
<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->
If `changeDetectionRef.detectChanges` is called in parent component during `ngOnChanges` hook of a child component then child's `ngAfterViewInit` hook is not called

**Expected behavior**
<!-- Describe what the behavior would be without the bug. -->
All hooks are called

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
<!--
If the current behavior is a bug or you can illustrate your feature request better with an example, 
please provide the *STEPS TO REPRODUCE* and if possible a *MINIMAL DEMO* of the problem via
https://plnkr.co or similar (you can use this template as a starting point: http://plnkr.co/edit/tpl:AvJOMERrnz94ekVua0u5).
-->
See console of the [plunker](https://plnkr.co/edit/T2WtlChLSmUMW5pVERXJ?p=preview)
If `detectChanges` is commented:
```
comp::ngOnInit
child::ngOnChanges
child::ngOnInit
child::ngAfterViewInit
comp::ngAfterViewInit
```
if not:
```
comp::ngOnInit
child::ngOnChanges
comp::ngAfterViewInit
```

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
<!-- Describe the motivation or the concrete use case -->
It's a bug

**Please tell us about your environment:**
<!-- Operating system, IDE, package manager, HTTP server, ... -->

* **Angular version:** 4.1.1+

* **Browser:** Chrome 58
<!-- All browsers where this could be reproduced -->
 
* **Language:** TypeScript 2.2

**Debug info**
May be it will help.
I tracked it down to these lines of `view.ts::checkAndUpdateView`:
```
  execComponentViewsAction(view, ViewAction.CheckAndUpdate);
  execQueriesAction(
      view, NodeFlags.TypeViewQuery, NodeFlags.DynamicQuery, CheckType.CheckAndUpdate);
  callLifecycleHooksChildrenFirst(
      view, NodeFlags.AfterViewChecked |
          (view.state & ViewState.FirstCheck ? NodeFlags.AfterViewInit : 0));
```

According to `view.state` it is a first check before calling `execComponentViewsAction` and it is not when `callLifecycleHooksChildrenFirst` is called.
